A protected wreck within local-authority boundaries is treated as a designated heritage asset for NPPF purposes.
Planning decisions afford such wrecks protection comparable to scheduled monuments and highly graded listed buildings.
The planning-consideration design page gives an expected record count of 57.
The protected-wreck consideration is expected to update fortnightly.
The first-return 1 m DSM is a raster elevation model.
The dataset covers approximately 99% of England.
The model is produced from the first or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The model includes object heights such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
Terrain is included where the first or only return was the ground.
The Environment Agency produced the composite in 2022.
The first-return composite is derived from National LiDAR Programme surveys.
The contributing survey period begins on 11 November 2016.
The contributing survey period ends on 5 May 2022.
The national programme divided England into approximately 300 survey blocks.
The programme surveyed blocks over continuous winters from 2016 onward.
Overlapping surveys are merged using a feathering technique.
Feathering removes small elevation differences between overlapping surveys.
First-return coverage does not exactly match the last-return DSM composite.
The dataset is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters.
GeoTIFF downloads are organised in 5 km tiles.
The composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
The first-return 2 m DSM is a raster elevation model.
The dataset covers approximately 99% of England.
It is produced from first-return or only-return LiDAR pulses.
The surface includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The dataset is derived from the National LiDAR Programme.
The programme used approximately 300 survey blocks.
Survey overlaps are merged with feathering.
The metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
The metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The metadata exposes a WCS service link.
The metadata links the first-return 2 m model to first-return 1 m and last-return DSM products.
The last-return DSM 2 m product is a raster elevation model.
It is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The Environment Agency produced the composite in 2022.
It combines the Time Stamped archive and National LiDAR Programme surveys.
The sources are merged and resampled to obtain the best possible coverage.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest suitable data is used.
Where repeat surveys exist, the best-resolution data is preferred.
The composite survey period begins on 6 June 2000.
The composite survey period ends on 2 April 2022.
The metadata states vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 cm RMSE.
The published coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The metadata exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API service resources.
The time-stamped DSM product is an archive of Environment Agency raster elevation data.
Site-specific surveys have been conducted across England since 1998.
